description: The release path (m21, m28): the host is reinstalled as Go v0.2.4 on Go's unit and leaves a run in flight; 0.3.0 takes over on the same unit and state and installs an LLM relay and a user-scoped public MCP connector with marked tokens; 0.4.0 takes over on its 0.4.0 unit, then the 0.5.0 candidate on the proposed 0.5.0 unit, each doing more work; then 0.4.0 is rolled back with its own unit. Each step reads the previous binary's records back and searches the host for the tokens.

inputs.agent: the dev VM's production-style system unit opute-bootstrap-mcp.service (Rust 0.5.0 release candidate binary, test identity e2e-devvm-agent, test token)
inputs.previous: the previous Rust releases, 0.4.0 (${PARITY}/e2e/release/rust-0.4.0-rc6) and 0.3.0 (${PARITY}/e2e/release/rust-0.3.0-rc9), copied in
inputs.slow: a local endpoint answering after 60 s (e2etool slow)

requirements.requirement: Forward: each release serves the previous release's state unchanged
requirements.scenario: Go v0.2.4's state, with a run stopped in flight, is served by 0.3.0; 0.3.0's state, with its relay, connector, plan and task, is served by 0.4.0; 0.4.0's by the 0.5.0 candidate: counts and ids reconcile per table and every record reads back with the status last reported
requirements.spec: openspec/changes/reimplement-host-agent-in-rust/milestones.md M12 (forward and rollback: Go rolled back onto Rust's state reports every task, Rust-era work included, with the status Rust last reported) and D1 (bit-compatible schema: conversion is the identity)

requirements.scenario: 0.4.0 started on 0.5.0's state, with its own 0.4.0 unit back, reads every operation, task and plan run, 0.5.0-era work included, with the status 0.5.0 last reported
requirements.spec: openspec/changes/reimplement-host-agent-in-rust/milestones.md M12 (forward and rollback: Go rolled back onto Rust's state reports every task, Rust-era work included, with the status Rust last reported) and D1 (bit-compatible schema: conversion is the identity)

requirements.scenario: Each release admits mutations from its unit: 0.3.0 from Go's unit, 0.4.0 from the 0.4.0 unit's setting, 0.5.0 from the 0.5.0 unit's --allow-mutations, and 0.4.0 again from its own unit after rollback

requirements.scenario: The relay's and the user-scoped connector's tokens, written under 0.3.0 and ensured again under 0.4.0, 0.5.0 and after rollback onto the same one connector, are in no journal line, no store row and no file that is not 0600 and the agent's user's, and in no process's environment; each connector call proves its origin and stops only at the unreachable public endpoint
